A process of a traditional Chinese medicine extract-combined feed for improving animal resistance. The specific procedures are as follows: S1: performing pre-cleaning on corn, sorghum and bean cake to remove impurities, removing magnet impurities by using a magnetic separator, putting the raw materials in a to-be-pulverized bin, pulverizing the raw materials in the to-be-pulverized bin by using a pulverizer and then distributing same to a raw material bin by means of a conveying device for storage, putting bran, fish meal, shell powder, table salt and bone meal, which do not require pulverizing, in a production workshop by means of a conveying device, performing pre-cleaning to remove impurities and removing magnet impurities by using a magnetic separator, and then distributing same to different batching bins for storage; S2: feeding 60-65 parts of corn, 6-7 parts of sorghum, 5-6 parts of bran, 20-25 parts of bean cake, 5-6 parts of fish meal, 0.3-0.4 part of shell powder, 0.3-0.4 part of table salt and 0.1-0.15 part of bone meal into a stirring device for mixing; S3, cleaning and drying all the medicinal materials, finally dividing the medicinal materials into the medicinal materials for long-term consumption and short-term consumption according to the formula of two feeds and storing the medicinal materials in different warehouses; S4: grinding the medicinal materials needed for the feed for long-term consumption, adding the medicinal material powder into an impregnation device, then adding Astragali radix polysaccharide, Natrii sulfas and medicated leaven, and adding dilute alcohol at the same time, impregnating the mixture for four days at 15℃-25℃, then filtering out the medicine residues and putting same into a pressing device, pressing the medicine residues by using the pressing device to obtain a pressing liquid, combining the pressing liquid with the filtrate, leaving the mixture to stand for 24 hours, filtering the liquid again, filtering out the precipitate to obtain an impregnation liquid, and concentrating the impregnation liquid by means of evaporation to obtain a liquid extract; S5: adding the liquid extract treated in step S4 into the stirring device in step S2, mixing same with the mixed feed, adding a certain number of maltose to improve the taste, and packing the mixed feed into sterilized packaging bags; and S6: pouring the medicinal materials needed for the feed for short-term consumption into a steamer, boiling same with equal amount of water, then filtering out liquid medicine for later use, pouring the liquid medicine into a mixing device, adding a certain amount of the feed of S2 into the mixing device at the same time, and adding maltose in proportion, mixing the liquid medicine, the mixed feed and the maltose to obtain a short-term feed, and preparing the short-term feed into particles with the diameter of one to two millimeters by means of granulation, then drying same, and finally packing the particles into sterilized packaging bags by means of a bagging machine.

The present invention relates to a method of trans-differentiating differentiated cells, the method comprising bringing said cells into contact with at least one component (i) and at least one component (ii), wherein said component (i) is selected from (a) a polypeptide comprising at least one domain selected from the group consisting of a BH1, a BH2, a BH3 and a BH4 domain; (b) a polypeptide comprising or consisting of the amino acid sequence of a wild-type form of a member of the Bcl-2 family or a fragment thereof; (c) a polypeptide comprising or consisting of the amino acid sequence of a wild-type form of a member of the Bcl-2 family or a fragment thereof, wherein said polypeptide comprises one or more point mutations as compared to said wild-type form or fragment thereof; (d) a polypeptide comprising or consisting of an amino acid sequence which sequence exhibits at least 30% sequence identity with a wild-type form of a member of the Bcl-2 family, said wild-type form of a member of the Bcl-2 family preferably being selected from the group consisting of human Bcl-2 (SEQ ID NO: 1 or 5), human Bcl-X L (SEQ ID NO: 6), human Bcl-w (SEQ ID NO: 7), human Mcl1 (SEQ ID NO: 8), human Bfl1 (SEQ ID NO: 9 or 10), human Nrh (SEQ ID NO: 11 ), human Bcl2L1 (SEQ ID NO: 12), human DIVA (SEQ ID NO: 13), human myeloid cell leukemia sequence 1 isoform 1 (SEQ ID NO: 14), and human Bcl-x beta (SEQ ID NO: 15); wherein said wild-type form has anti-apoptotic activity; a nucleic acid encoding said polypeptide; and means for enhancing the amount and/or activity of said polypeptide in said cells; wherein said component (i) enhances the yield of trans-differentiated cells by at least 30% as compared to the absence of said component (i); and wherein said component (ii) is selected from a transcription factor capable of trans-differentiating said cells; a nucleic acid encoding said transcription factor; and means for enhancing the amount and/or activity of said transcription factor in said cells; wherein any method of treatment of the human or animal body by therapy is excluded. In a second aspect, the present invention provides a combination comprising or consisting of (a) at least one component (i) and at least one component (ii); (b) at least one component (iii) and at least one component (ii); or (c) at least one component (i), at least one component (ii), and at least one component (iii); each of said components being as defined above. For components (i), (ii) and (iii)(a), nucleic acids are preferred.

The organic matter carbonization process is based on thermal treatment at high temperatures, under a controlled atmosphere, if possible in the absence of oxygen. The organic matter carbonization theory was expounded in this text, with emphasis on the thermodynamic aspects. It is shown in this exposition the important misfit between the endothermic and the exothermic carbonization stages, which hinders the use of the energy emitted during the exothermic stage by the brick kilns. Following there is a summary of the carbonization technique actual stage. The present invention relates to a method and plant for the thermal treatment of organic matter comprising independent reactors for the drying and pyrolysis of organic matter, and an independent reactor for the charcoal cooling. In this method the volatile products - non condensable gases and condensable pyrolytic vapors - are burned in an independent combustion chamber in order to supply the energy demanded by the process. In this way wood is not burned, and polluting substances are not emitted to the atmosphere. The method proposed by the present invention allows a precise control of the process in order to obtain the specified charcoal fixed carbon content; and a higher gravimetric yield, which gives an increase of the forest wood, either native or cultivated. In the independent pyrolysis and drying reactors proposed by the present invention, exiting flue gases from an external combustion chamber are driven to the drying reactor where the wood onto roll on buckets are heated and dried. Fuel gases emitted by the carbonizing wood are burned in the combustion chamber as an energy source. Inside the combustion chamber is placed a heat exchanger with the aim to reheat the pyrolytic gases. After reheated, these gases return to the carbonizing reactor in order to supply energy for the endothermic carbonizing step. The aim of this technique is to avoid the mixing of the fuel gases with the flue gases generated inside the combustion chamber, and to precisely control the carbonizing temperature. The present invention allows the production of intermediate products between wet wood and charcoal by halting the carbonization process at the desired stage in order to obtain anhydrous wood, char or, or high volatile content charcoal. The basic concepts of the process are: 1 - Utilization of the emitted gases by the carbonizing wood as an energy source. 2 - The stages of wood drying, wood pyrolysis and charcoal cooling are performed in independent reactors, inside which only one of these stages occurs. 3 - Energy supply during the carbonizing endothermic stage of the pyrolysis by the gases emitted during this stage after reheated in a heat exchanger. Basically the present invention comprises the following equipments: 1 — Reaction chambers inside which the process stages are performed. 2 — An external combustion chamber. 3- A heat exchanger inside said combustion chamber. 4 - A set of pipes. 5 - A set of fans. 6 - A loading system comprising roll on buckets.

The invention relates to medicine, in particular to methods for individual selection (screening) of therapeutic agents both drug preparations and non-medicated agents for a specific patient and for different human diseases (inflammatory, oncological, immunodifficient, infectious etc). Said invention increases the accuracy of selection of required remedies, optimises doses and combinations thereof, thereby improving the therapeutic effect. The invention also extends the medical capabilities of a therapy by performing it out with the aid of non-medicated methods. The inventive method for individual selection of remedies for a specific patient consists in culturing blood components of the patient in tested remedies, analysing substrates of blood components prior and after culturing, determining the concentration ratio between thiols (-SH) groups and disulphide (-SS-) groups in a cellular fraction (thiols-disulphide ratio TDR) and in selecting the optimal remedy. The culturing of the blood components of the patient is carried out during time periods of 24-72 hours, the TDR being determined at intervals of 30-120 minutes. Afterwards, a TDR-time chart is constructed, the selection of the optimal remedy being performed by comparing areas below the charts. Said areas are calculated using the TDR data and the time of culturing. The blood components of the patient are simultaneously cultured in several remedies. The cellular fraction produced from citrated blood is cultured. A tested preparation is used during the selection of the drug preparation for culturing the blood components of the patient. Said tested preparation is used taking account of the bioavailability thereof with respect to different ways of its introduction in the organism (intramuscular, intravenous, enteral) and the sex and weight of the patient. The selection of non-medication agents as the remedies and the dosage thereof are carried out as follows: for high-power remedies (inductothermy, antitumoral radiotherapy) the time of action on a blood sample of the patient is chosen in such away that they are as many times less than the time of therapy, as the volume of sample is less than the volume of tissues which are exposed to radiation during the cure of a human being. For ultralow-power remedies having mainly the information and correction effect (energy-information therapy), the time of action on a blood sample of the patient is chosen such that it is equal to the duration of the therapeutical procedure. When anti-infective and antitumoral medicamental chemical preparations, an antitumoral radio therapy and the remedies are used for a direct distruction of an infective agent or a tumor cell, the medicamental preparations and non medicated agents are selected with respect to the lesser area below time theTDR-culturing chart. When the immunomodulating, bracing and information correction medicamental preparations and non-medicated agents are used, they are selected in relation to the larger area below theTDR-culturing chart.
